measurement_caveats.order_bias_bound: The shipping C8 +0.7% single same-chain pair is inside the measured second-arm order band (candidate-first vs control-first prefill A/B at rows 16/45 spans +0.01% to -0.84% on a dispatch-identical control), so that 0.7% is not separable from arm order and must not be quoted as an independent speed win.

measurement_caveats.server_pair_provenance: Corrected 2026-08-30, superseding an earlier caveat of mine that mislabelled this axis. The cited +0.7% pair IS reproducible: summary.8.ar.tok_s = 45.618 in /tmp/he-server-rep2-512.json (2026-08-30T00:29:10Z, floor 512, fused owner off) and 45.936 in /tmp/he-server-rep2-16.json (2026-08-30T00:32:31Z, shipped floor 16, owner on); both widths [1,8] x 10 prompts on the same protocol, with C1 21.966 -> 21.954 (-0.05%, flat) and C8 MTP 31.512 -> 31.573 (+0.19%). The other pair I first reached for is NOT the promotion contrast: /tmp/he-uneq-srv-33.json vs /tmp/he-uneq16-shipped.json varies floor 33 vs 16, and both floors admit the owner at every width of this protocol, so 46.062 -> 45.999 (-0.14%) is a dispatch-identical server control. One -0.14% control draw against one +0.70% candidate draw at the same width and protocol puts same-protocol packet drift at roughly the 0.8-point level, so the C8 AR gain is not separable from packet drift or arm order at one packet per arm. C8 AR is therefore recorded as unresolved, not as a win; the promotion rests on byte-identical arithmetic (20/20 packed trajectory hashes, both measurement orders) and the order-controlled +1.81% packed prefill crossover.
